Replicating SGR with probly: CIFAR-10 and ImageNet

Status of the replication of Geifman and El-Yaniv (2017), Sec. 5: CIFAR-10 (Table 1) and ImageNet (Tables 3-6, Fig. 2c), implementation differences, and further comparisons on CIFAR-10.

1. Summary

  • CIFAR-10 (Table 1). The coverage ranking of the paper holds. Cutting the threshold at the paper's test risk gives 0.8 to 2.1 points more coverage than the paper; SGR at delta = 0.001 gives 1.2 to 1.8 points less for r* of 0.02 and above. At r* = 0.01 SGR certifies 60% of the splits.
  • Printed bounds. Recomputed from the paper's own train numbers, the bound B* of Lemma 3.1 does not match the printed one in any CIFAR-10 row (implied delta 0.01 to 0.12).
  • Guarantee. SGR at delta = 0.001 exceeded the target in none of the 50 seed x split pairs for the methods in this report. The empirical threshold exceeds it in about half of the splits.
  • Deep ensemble. Five members with the same SGR rule reach 79.4% coverage at r* = 0.01 (paper: 78.6%; softmax: 23.9%).
  • ImageNet (Tables 3-6). Accuracies match torchvision's published ones (VGG-16 71.6% top-1, ResNet-50 76.1%). The VGG-16 risk-coverage curve lies close to the paper's test points (mean |risk difference| 0.0073 top-1, 0.0037 top-5). Our ResNet-50 curve gives 3.3 to 6.6 points more coverage at the paper's risk, so it is likely not the paper's model and its tables are not a like-for-like comparison.
  • ImageNet, bounds. The printed bounds do not follow from Lemma 3.1 either (implied delta 0.01 to 0.11), and the paper's train risks lie at or above our delta = 0.1 values in 26 of 26 rows. SGR at delta = 0.001 accepts more than the paper in 20 of 26 rows and exceeded the target on the test half in at most 2% of the splits (test-set noise, see section 5), the empirical threshold in 57% to 62% at the worst r* per table.
  • Fig. 2c reproduces. Risk at 60% coverage (VGG-16 top-1): SR 0.088, MC variance 0.171 (paper: about 0.10 and above 0.20); MC max-prob, not in the paper, 0.089.
  • Not done. CIFAR-100 (Table 2), Keras weights and Keras preprocessing.

2. Setup

CIFAR-10: the 10,000 test images are split 10 times at random into 5,000 selection and 5,000 test images; every number is a mean over 5 training seeds x 10 splits = 50 pairs. ImageNet: 100 random halvings of the 50,000 validation images (25,000 / 25,000), pretrained torchvision models. The paper used a single split. delta = 0.001 throughout, as in the paper. A split is certified if the rule found a threshold with bound at most r*; otherwise nothing is accepted. Violation is the share of certified splits whose test risk exceeds r*. It is measured on the finite test half, while the guarantee concerns the true risk, so test-set noise alone can produce a few violations.

probly components: SGRSelector, CoverageSelector and ThresholdSelector for the thresholds; risk_coverage_curve, aurc and coverage_at_risk from probly.metrics.selective_prediction (CIFAR-10 additionally AUGRC).

Glossary
SR
Softmax response: the highest softmax probability, the paper's score. Called softmax in the CIFAR-10 sections.
MC variance
Variance of the predicted class's probability over the MC-dropout passes (the paper's MC-dropout score).
MC max-prob
Highest probability of the mean MC-dropout prediction.
1 - top-5 mass
One minus the summed probability of the five most likely classes (score for the top-5 loss).
r*, delta
Target risk, and the allowed probability that the true risk of the returned rule exceeds it.
B*
The SGR bound of Lemma 3.1 at the returned threshold.
Implied delta
The delta at which B*, recomputed from the paper's printed train numbers, equals the printed bound.
Coverage at the paper's risk
Coverage of our risk-coverage curve at the paper's printed test risk, independent of any threshold rule.
Empirical threshold
Largest coverage whose selection-set risk is below r*, without a bound.
AURC, AUGRC
Area under the risk-coverage curve and under the generalized risk-coverage curve (Traub et al., 2024); lower is better.

4. Replication, CIFAR-10 (Table 1)

Table 1 of the paper gives, per target risk r*, the test coverage of SGR with a VGG-16. The comparison uses the paper model (VGG-16 with dropout, softmax score).

r*PaperOurs, at the paper's riskOurs, SGR delta = 0.001Certified splits
0.0178.6%80.6%38.2%60%
0.0284.7%85.5%83.4%100%
0.0596.0%96.9%94.2%100%

Cut at the paper's test risk, our curve accepts 0.8 to 2.1 points more than the paper. SGR at delta = 0.001 ends 1.2 to 1.8 points below it for r* of 0.02 and above. SGR at delta = 0.1 gives 85.2% at r* = 0.02, close to the paper (see section 6). At r* = 0.01 the bound is met on 60% of the splits, so the mean coverage (38.2%) has a large spread.

Returning the last tested iterate as in Algorithm 1 (sgr_last_tested) instead of the last certified one returns a threshold on every split, but on the splits where SGRSelector abstains that threshold accepts almost nothing, so the mean coverage at r* = 0.01 is the same (38.2% for both).

5. Replication, ImageNet (Tables 3-6, Fig. 2c)

Protocol: 100 halvings of the validation set; the first half selects the threshold at each r* of the paper's table, the second half measures test risk and coverage. Losses are top-1 and top-5 error. Both models are torchvision weights (VGG-16, ResNet-50). The score is SR (softmax response) unless stated otherwise.

Paper tableAccuracyAURC (SR)Mean |risk difference|Coverage difference at the paper's risk (points)
3: VGG-16 top-171.6%0.08870.00730.5 to 2.6
4: VGG-16 top-590.4%0.02300.00371.7 to 3.1
5: ResNet-50 top-176.1%0.06970.01853.3 to 5.6
6: ResNet-50 top-592.9%0.01720.00603.3 to 6.6

The line-up compares our risk-coverage curve with the paper's test points independently of SGR: risk at the paper's coverage, and coverage at the paper's risk. VGG-16 is the relevant comparison. ResNet-50 (V1 weights) gives 3.3 to 6.6 points more coverage than the paper at the same risk in every row, so it is likely not the paper's model. Its accuracy (76.1%) does not settle this: Table 5 only bounds the paper's top-1 accuracy to 72.6% to 76.4%.

SGR at delta = 0.001 against the paper

Paper tablePaper coverage (smallest / largest r*)SGR 0.001SGR 0.1Violating splits, SGR (worst r*)Violating splits, empirical (worst r*)
3: VGG-16 top-123.2% / 91.2%23.3% / 92.2%26.2% / 92.9%0%59%
4: VGG-16 top-533.4% / 91.1%22.2% / 91.8%30.7% / 92.6%2%61%

6: ResNet-50 top-538.1% / 94.8%28.6% / 98.5%36.6% / 99.0%2%57%

SGR at delta = 0.001 accepts more than the paper in 20 of 26 rows, in line with our curves lying at or above the paper's points. It accepts less in the other 6 rows, all at r* = 0.04 or below, by up to 11.2 points (Table 4 at r* = 0.01: 22.2% against 33.4%); there, SGR at delta = 0.1 comes within 2.7 points of the paper. At most 2% of the splits exceed r* on the test half. This does not break the guarantee, which concerns the true risk: the test risk of a split varies with a standard deviation of 0.0013 to 0.0041 over splits, so a threshold close to r* can exceed it on the test half. The empirical threshold accepts more still and exceeds r* in 57% to 62% of the splits at the worst r* per table.

The paper reports for VGG-16 top-1 at 60% coverage about 10% error with SR and more than 20% with MC dropout, and calls SR significantly better on both losses. This reproduces: with the variance of the MC samples as score (the paper's MC-dropout criterion), risk at 60% coverage is 0.171 against 0.088 for top-1 and 0.065 against 0.020 for top-5 (VGG-16). The max probability of the mean MC prediction, which the paper does not use, is about as good as SR (0.089).

Score for the top-5 loss

The paper uses SR for both losses. The score 1 - top-5 mass matches the top-5 loss and is better on the whole curve; SGR coverage at r* = 0.01 is 41.5% against 22.2% (VGG-16) and 43.0% against 28.6% (ResNet-50); at r* = 0.02 63.6% against 52.4% and 72.8% against 60.0%.

7. Uncertainty methods (CIFAR-10)

Ranking quality by AURC and AUGRC (left) and what the methods deliver under SGR (table).

MethodAURC x1000AUGRC x1000SGR coverage, r* 0.02Certified, r* 0.01
Softmax (base model)8.946.5983.4%34%
MC dropout, max prob6.695.9283.3%100%
Deep ensemble, max prob5.904.5487.1%100%
Deep ensemble, epistemic5.394.7386.4%100%
Paper model, softmax8.686.6483.4%60%

The deep ensemble has the lowest AUGRC (4.54, softmax 6.59) and the highest guaranteed coverage. MC dropout (5.92, 100 passes) samples from the base model fine-tuned with dropout layers; a single deterministic pass of that model, not in the table, gives 5.95, so the gain over the softmax comes from the fine-tuning, not from the sampling. The paper model (trained from scratch with dropout) is a different model. The ensemble's epistemic score has the lowest AURC, while AUGRC and SGR coverage favor its max-probability score. SWA, SWAG, DDU, VBLL, SNGP and Laplace (appendix) are not better than the softmax; these were fine-tuned for 20 epochs at learning rate 0.01 from the base model and end below its accuracy (0.916-0.926 against 0.9375), so the comparison also reflects training budget.

8. Threshold rules (CIFAR-10)

Coverage per threshold rule for the deep ensemble; the share of violating splits is written next to rules without a guarantee.

Rule (deep ensemble, r* = 0.02)GuaranteeCoverageViolating splits
SGRyes87.1%0%
Learn-then-Test, fixed sequenceyes86.8%0%
Fixed sequence, splityes86.8%0%
Learn-then-Test, Bonferroniyes86.1%0%
Empirical (no guarantee)no90.9%50%
Conformal singletonsno88.2%10%
Softmax cutoff 1 - r*no83.3%0%

SGR, Learn-then-Test with a fixed sequence and the split fixed-sequence rule give nearly the same coverage; the Bonferroni variant is 0.8 to 1.6 points below SGR. The empirical threshold accepts the most and violates the target in 40% to 50% of the splits. The conformal rule accepts more than SGR and violated in at most 10% of the splits for the ensemble, without a guarantee. The softmax cutoff 1 - r* was safe in these runs but accepts less at larger r* (86.1% at r* = 0.05 against 96.7% for SGR).

9. Deep ensemble + SGR (CIFAR-10)

Deep ensemble of five with the plain SGR rule at delta = 0.001, against the paper's reported coverage (which rests on a weaker bound, section 6).

r*PaperSoftmax + SGREnsemble + SGRResNet-18 softmax + SGRResNet-18 ensemble + SGR
0.0178.6%23.9%79.4%52.9%83.0%
0.0284.7%83.4%87.1%88.1%92.0%
0.0596.0%94.3%96.7%97.3%98.9%

VGG-16, r* = 0.01: ensemble 79.4% coverage, certified on 100% of the splits (paper: 78.6%; softmax 23.9%, certified on 34%). ResNet-18: 83.0% against 52.9%.

Cost

At r* = 0.01 two members reach 75.7% coverage, 100 MC dropout passes 73.3%, five members 79.4%. The ResNet-18 cost sweep was not run (its saved predictions are not available).
